run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-14T20:58:24Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by 504 responses that frontend-proxy returns for POST /api/checkout only. Its ingress spans carry http.status_code 504 / status ERROR at ~15.0 s, its access log shows '504 UT response_timeout' at 14999-15001 ms, and the error-span rate rose from ~0.011/s (20:34-20:56) to 0.211/s at 20:58:24, 0.4/s at 21:02:24 and 0.5/s at 21:08:24. The frontend's own /api/checkout handling did not fail but became slow: p50 130-180 ms before, 10.1 s in the 21:00 bucket and 15 s (highest finite bucket) at 21:05/21:10; the slow segment is checkout's Kafka producer span 'orders publish' (p50 1 ms through 20:55, then 10.6 s / 15 s), while every other checkout downstream operation (PaymentService/Charge ~1.2 ms, CartService ~1.3 ms, CurrencyService ~1.3 ms, ProductCatalogService ~1.1 ms) stayed flat. Checkout logs confirm the write path itself: 'Successful to write message ... duration: 11.4-19.2s' at 21:05, and earlier a broker outage window (20:56:13-20:57:25 'dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused', 'circuit breaker is open') that recovered at 20:57:38. The only change matching this onset is the Kafka Deployment: pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-14T20:55:53Z, revision 2, new ReplicaSet kafka-5c9d7cc485 replacing kafka-ff7884766 with an identical image/args/env/resources and no volumes; the restarted broker re-created topic orders at 20:57:31-34 with high watermark 0. So the alert is a downstream symptom of the Kafka rollout restart and the resulting slow checkout produce path, converted into 504s by frontend-proxy's fixed 15 s upstream timeout. Groups: affected - frontend-proxy (own 504 error spans/error rate), checkout (own ERROR publish spans and 11-19 s write durations), frontend (own slow /api/checkout server spans, no errors seen); the change this cause traces to - Kafka Deployment rollout restart at 20:55:53; changed during the window for other reasons - fraud-detection container OOMKilled/restarted at 20:48:58 and restarted flagd Deployment at 20:24:34, neither tied to these 504s; checked and healthy - all 5 nodes (Ready, no pressure), checkout/kafka container CPU/memory (no throttling, far below limits), kafka Service endpoints. The broker-internal reason that produce acks take 11-19 s after recovery is not established from available signals and remains a gap.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error-span rate (STATUS_CODE_ERROR) was 0.011/s at 20:34-20:36 and 0.044/s at 20:54, then 0.2111/s at 20:58:24, 0.2169/s at 21:00:24, 0.4/s at 21:02:24, 0.4333/s at 21:04-21:06 and 0.5/s at 21:08:24; the errors are on span 'ingress' only ('router frontend egress' error series is 0).

In the per-service error-span rate, frontend-proxy is the only service with a sustained material error rate (0.39999 at the 21:00:24 point, matching the alert's reported current value 0.39999999999999997); the only other non-zero point is checkout at 0.1598/s at 20:58:24, after which its points are 0.

Sampled frontend-proxy error spans are operation 'ingress' (span kind server) with status tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR and durations ~15,000,000-15,012,259 us; their child 'router frontend egress' client spans carry error=true and http.status_code=0 at ~15 s, and the parent spans of service load-generator (operation 'POST') also show 504.

frontend-proxy access log lines show '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout' with request durations 14999-15001 ms; the 30 newest matching lines cover 21:03:53-21:05:12 and 166 such 504 lines exist in 20:55-21:11.

The frontend server span 'POST /api/checkout' in one of these traces completed after 21.57 s with http.status_code=200, i.e. the frontend finished the request after frontend-proxy had already returned 504 at 15 s.

frontend p50 latency for 'POST /api/checkout' and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' was 130-180 ms in the 20:35-20:55 buckets, 10083 ms in the 21:00 bucket and 15000 ms (highest finite histogram bucket) in the 21:05 and 21:10 buckets, while other frontend operations (GET /, GET /api/cart, GET /api/products/{productId}, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations) stayed in the low-millisecond range.

checkout p50 latency for the producer span 'orders publish' was 1 ms in the 20:35-20:55 buckets, 10620.7 ms in the 21:00 bucket and 15000 ms in the 21:05 and 21:10 buckets; 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' went from 97-150 ms to 9500 ms and 15000 ms over the same points, while all other checkout operations stayed flat (oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 1.23-1.47 ms, CartService/GetCart 1.18-1.46 ms, CartService/EmptyCart 3.0-16.2 ms, CurrencyService/Convert 1.25-1.45 ms, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 1.04-1.19 ms, prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart 50-72 ms).

'orders publish' duration buckets: at 20:50 the whole rate 0.536/s sat in le=2 ms (all buckets above 2 ms equal 0.536/s, i.e. no slower samples); at 21:08 buckets le<=8000 were 0, le=10000 0.0186/s, le=15000 0.1974/s and +Inf 0.4805/s, so ~59% of publishes were slower than 15 s.

checkout application log lines at 21:05:11-21:05:34 report 'Successful to write message. offset: 0, duration: 17.011844752s', 17.232028861s, 19.20032921s, 16.896968671s, 12.356581096s, 11.452121497s and similar values, i.e. the Kafka write call itself took 11-19 s while still succeeding.

checkout logs from 20:56:13 to 20:57:25 show repeated 'Failed to connect to broker kafka:9092: dial tcp 100.65.62.181:9092: connect: connection refused', 'Failed to write message: kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to' and 'Failed to write message: circuit breaker is open', then at 20:57:38 'Connected to broker at kafka:9092 (registered as #1)'.

Over the authorized window checkout recorded 14.7 'orders publish' spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR and 1267 with STATUS_CODE_UNSET, while its 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' server spans are all STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no checkout server errors).

The Kafka Deployment is at revision 2 with pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-14T20:55:53Z; events show Deployment 'kafka' ScalingReplicaSet up kafka-5c9d7cc485 and down kafka-ff7884766, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate of pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 at 20:55:53 and SuccessfulDelete of kafka-ff7884766-pn5m2 at 20:55:55; that pod was Scheduled and its kafka container Started at 20:55:53-20:55:54.

The old and new Kafka ReplicaSet pod templates are identical in image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-kafka), args (none), env (KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092, KAFKA_HEAP_OPTS -Xmx400M -Xms400M, KAFKA_LISTENERS PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093, KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS 1@kafka:9093, etc.) and resources (limits cpu 400m / memory 900Mi, requests cpu 100m / memory 300Mi); neither template declares any volume, so /tmp/kafka-logs is container-local.

The restarted broker's log shows the orders topic being auto-created by the client request: 'CreateTopics result(s): CreatableTopic(name=orders, numPartitions=1, replicationFactor=1 ...): SUCCESS' at 20:57:31, 'Creating new partition orders-0' at 20:57:34 and 'Log loaded for partition orders-0 with initial high watermark 0'.
The kafka Service endpoints resolve correctly to the new pod: address 100.96.4.3 with targetRef Pod kafka-5c9d7cc485-hrd97 and ports plaintext 9092 and controller 9093.

In the kafka container logs read from 20:55 to 21:05:22 (1344 lines) no ERROR, WARN, FATAL or Exception line matched; the only matches for the broader pattern were the orders topic auto-creation lines of 20:57:31-20:57:34.

Container resource readings: kafka CPU was 0.012-0.025 cores on the old pod and 0.098 (20:56:24), 0.246 (20:58:24) then 0.0136-0.029 cores on the new pod, with CFS throttled-period ratio 1.0 at 20:56:24 and 0.588 at 20:58:24 during startup and 0.003-0.020 afterwards; kafka working set was 613-622 MB against a 900Mi limit; checkout used 12.7-13.4 MB against a 512Mi limit with CFS throttled-period ratio 0 across 20:37-21:07.
All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with restart count 0 except fraud-detection (2 restarts); the frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bh295 is Running/Ready with 0 restarts.
All 5 nodes report Ready=True with NetworkUnavailable, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False, so no node-level resource pressure is present.

Among the 21 deployments only two carry a pod-template restartedAt annotation: flagd (2026-11-14T20:24:34Z, revision 2) and kafka (2026-11-14T20:55:53Z, revision 2); every deployment reports ready 1 of 1 with no unavailable replicas.

Separately, the fraud-detection container has restartCount 2 and its last termination was reason OOMKilled with exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-14T20:48:58Z; the container restarted at 20:49:12 and is currently running and Ready.

Causal chain: the Kafka Deployment rollout restart at 20:55:53 (broker unavailable ~20:55:53-20:57:38) made checkout's produce calls fail with connection-refused/circuit-breaker and afterwards run at 11-19 s per write to topic orders; POST /api/checkout therefore takes 15-21 s, exceeding frontend-proxy's 15 s upstream response timeout, so frontend-proxy returns 504 UT response_timeout on 'ingress' and RequestErrorRate fires.

The restart also wiped the single broker's topic data (pod templates declare no volume, so /tmp/kafka-logs is container-local) and topic orders had to be re-created at 20:57:31-34 with high watermark 0; this coincides with the persistent 11-19 s produce latency, but the mechanism by which a fresh single-partition log yields multi-second acks is not established by the evidence.

frontend-proxy's fixed 15 s route/upstream timeout is the immediate conversion mechanism rather than a fault of its own: it is unchanged (Deployment revision 1, pod 0 restarts, only /api/checkout returns 504 while GET/POST /api/cart, /api/products, /api/data, /api/recommendations return 200), and the frontend server span for the same request still completes with status 200 after 15-21 s.
Node-level resource pressure is rejected as a cause: all 5 nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False.

CPU/memory starvation of the checkout client or of the broker is rejected as the driver of the latency: checkout showed CFS throttle ratio 0 and 12.7-13.4 MB of 512Mi, and the kafka container used 0.0136-0.029 cores with ~2% throttled periods after startup, far below its 400m limit, while produce calls took 11-19 s.

A Kafka Service/endpoint misconfiguration (stale pod address or wrong target port) is rejected: the endpoints object lists the new pod 100.96.4.3 with plaintext port 9092 and controller port 9093, and checkout successfully reconnected to kafka:9092 at 20:57:38 after the connection refusals.

The fraud-detection container's OOMKill at 20:48:58 is rejected as the cause of these 504s: it occurred before the Kafka restart and the latency jump, fraud-detection's per-service error-span rate points in this window are 0, and the slow segment of the affected requests is checkout's kafka 'orders publish' span, not a fraud-detection call (it does not appear in checkout's operation list).

The broker itself shows no error signal for the slow period: its CPU is at baseline, its logs contain no ERROR/WARN/FATAL/Exception lines and it completed the topic creation successfully, so 'Kafka is failing' is not directly proven by broker-side error evidence - only the client-side 11-19 s write durations show the slowness.

The 15000 ms latency values are the highest finite bucket of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, so they mean 'at least 15 s', not an exact 15 s; exact durations come only from the sampled spans (e.g. 21.48 s PlaceOrder, 21.33 s orders publish) and not from the quantiles.

Have a Kafka owner inspect broker/controller internals for the post-restart period (produce request queue time, request-handler latency, disk/fsync latency on the container-local /tmp/kafka-logs, server.properties values) and consider giving the broker a persistent volume so a restart no longer discards topic data; no such internal metrics exist in the available Prometheus data.

Review the frontend-proxy 15 s upstream timeout against checkout's expected worst-case latency (or bound the Kafka produce time in checkout so it fails fast), and investigate the separate fraud-detection OOMKilled container (memory limit vs. usage) as its own issue.

gaps: The broker-internal reason that checkout's produce calls take 11-19 s after the restart is not established: no Kafka JMX/broker-request/disk-latency metrics are present in the available Prometheus data, and the kafka log read ends at 21:05:22 (1344 lines), so later broker state is unknown.
Only 30 of 166 frontend-proxy 504 access-log lines and 60 of 492 frontend-proxy error spans were read; whether every 504 in the window is POST /api/checkout is unknown beyond the sampled slice.
Series data ends around 21:08-21:10 (data_as_of of the metric queries), so the current state of the error rate and latency after that is unknown.

The change_history integration is not available, so what triggered the Kafka pod-template restart (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-14T20:55:53Z) and whether any Kafka configuration value changed cannot be verified; secrets/configuration contents are not readable.

frontend's own application logs yielded no readable lines (0 lines read) for the filtered query, so frontend-side log evidence for the /api/checkout latency is missing; the frontend's CFS throttle ratio was not queried.
The flagd Deployment restart at 20:24:34 was not examined in logs, and flagd's absence from the returned error-span series is unknown rather than proven zero.

Only the kafka, checkout, frontend-proxy and fraud-detection pods were inspected in depth; other services' logs and per-operation latency (email, accounting, shipping, ad, recommendation, payment beyond checkout's Charge span) were not individually verified.
next_steps: For a Kafka operator: capture broker request-handler and log-append/fsync latency, request queue size and any produce throttle-time metrics for 20:55-21:11, and confirm why a single-partition topic with high watermark 0 served produce acks in 11-19 s.

Check whether the kafka Deployment restart at 20:55:53 was a planned rollout restart and whether /tmp/kafka-logs data loss (no volume) is acceptable; plan persistent storage or a topic-recovery check.
Align or explicitly bound the frontend-proxy 15 s route timeout with checkout's Kafka write deadline so a stalled write yields a fast, visible error instead of client 504s.
Investigate the fraud-detection OOMKilled container (exit 137, 20:48:58) separately, including its memory limit and usage profile.
Re-run the same queries after the incident to confirm the frontend-proxy error span rate returns to the ~0.01-0.04/s baseline once produce latency recovers.

recommendation.text: Have a Kafka owner inspect broker/controller internals for the post-restart period (produce request queue time, request-handler latency, disk/fsync latency on the container-local /tmp/kafka-logs, server.properties values) and consider giving the broker a persistent volume so a restart no longer discards topic data; no such internal metrics exist in the available Prometheus data.

Review the frontend-proxy 15 s upstream timeout against checkout's expected worst-case latency (or bound the Kafka produce time in checkout so it fails fast), and investigate the separate fraud-detection OOMKilled container (memory limit vs. usage) as its own issue.

counter_evidence.text: The broker itself shows no error signal for the slow period: its CPU is at baseline, its logs contain no ERROR/WARN/FATAL/Exception lines and it completed the topic creation successfully, so 'Kafka is failing' is not directly proven by broker-side error evidence - only the client-side 11-19 s write durations show the slowness.

The 15000 ms latency values are the highest finite bucket of traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, so they mean 'at least 15 s', not an exact 15 s; exact durations come only from the sampled spans (e.g. 21.48 s PlaceOrder, 21.33 s orders publish) and not from the quantiles.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Node-level resource pressure is rejected as a cause: all 5 nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False.

CPU/memory starvation of the checkout client or of the broker is rejected as the driver of the latency: checkout showed CFS throttle ratio 0 and 12.7-13.4 MB of 512Mi, and the kafka container used 0.0136-0.029 cores with ~2% throttled periods after startup, far below its 400m limit, while produce calls took 11-19 s.

A Kafka Service/endpoint misconfiguration (stale pod address or wrong target port) is rejected: the endpoints object lists the new pod 100.96.4.3 with plaintext port 9092 and controller port 9093, and checkout successfully reconnected to kafka:9092 at 20:57:38 after the connection refusals.

The fraud-detection container's OOMKill at 20:48:58 is rejected as the cause of these 504s: it occurred before the Kafka restart and the latency jump, fraud-detection's per-service error-span rate points in this window are 0, and the slow segment of the affected requests is checkout's kafka 'orders publish' span, not a fraud-detection call (it does not appear in checkout's operation list).
